_meta.terminology: Direction of Integration (growth) and Direction of Disintegration (stress). Movement is keyed to the Levels of Development: healthy-level traits are taken on toward the integration point; average-to-unhealthy-level traits are taken on toward the disintegration point. Integration is framed as conscious and chosen; disintegration as involuntary and stress-driven. Distinct from the 'security point / stress point' language used by Palmer and others, and from Naranjo's differing group assignments.
_meta.arrow_geometry: 1-4-2-8-5-7 hexad (from the repeating decimal of 1/7) run one way for disintegration and reversed for integration, plus the 3-6-9 triangle run in opposite directions.
sources: Riso, Don Richard, & Hudson, Russ. Personality Types: Using the Enneagram for Self-Discovery. Rev. ed. Houghton Mifflin, 1996.
Riso, Don Richard, & Hudson, Russ. The Wisdom of the Enneagram. Bantam, 1999.
The Enneagram Institute, type descriptions, enneagraminstitute.com.

arrows.integration_text: The self-controlled, resentful One relaxes its inner critic and becomes spontaneous, joyful, and open to pleasure and experience, accepting life as it is.
arrows.disintegration_text: Under stress the One takes on average-to-unhealthy Four traits: moody, self-absorbed, self-pitying, sinking into melancholy and feeling misunderstood.
arrows.source: Riso & Hudson, Personality Types (rev. 1996) & The Wisdom of the Enneagram (1999); enneagraminstitute.com. [STRUCTURE]. Exact pages CANNOT VERIFY.

arrows.integration_text: The prideful, self-effacing Two turns inward and owns its own emotions and needs, nurturing itself instead of living through others.
arrows.disintegration_text: Under stress the Two takes on average-to-unhealthy Eight traits: repressed anger and entitlement erupt as aggression, coercion, and open demand.
arrows.source: Riso & Hudson, Personality Types (rev. 1996) & The Wisdom of the Enneagram (1999); enneagraminstitute.com. [STRUCTURE]. Exact pages CANNOT VERIFY.

arrows.integration_text: The image-driven Three moves from self-interest into genuine commitment, cooperation, and loyalty to something beyond personal success.
arrows.disintegration_text: Under stress the Three takes on average-to-unhealthy Nine traits: disengaged, numb, apathetic, procrastinating and dissociating when achievement stalls.
arrows.source: Riso & Hudson, Personality Types (rev. 1996) & The Wisdom of the Enneagram (1999); enneagraminstitute.com. [STRUCTURE]. Exact pages CANNOT VERIFY.

arrows.integration_text: The volatile, self-absorbed Four becomes objective, principled, and disciplined, translating vision into concrete work and tolerating structure.
arrows.disintegration_text: Under stress the Four takes on average-to-unhealthy Two traits: clinging, dependent, and over-involved, seeking love by being needed and losing itself.
arrows.source: Riso & Hudson, Personality Types (rev. 1996) & The Wisdom of the Enneagram (1999); enneagraminstitute.com. [STRUCTURE]. Exact pages CANNOT VERIFY.

arrows.integration_text: The withdrawn Five moves from thought into action, grounding in the body and engaging the world with confidence and decisive authority.
arrows.disintegration_text: Under stress the Five takes on average-to-unhealthy Seven traits: scattered, hyperactive, and impulsive, jumping between distractions to escape emptiness.
arrows.source: Riso & Hudson, Personality Types (rev. 1996) & The Wisdom of the Enneagram (1999); enneagraminstitute.com. [STRUCTURE]. Exact pages CANNOT VERIFY.

arrows.integration_text: The anxious, reactive Six settles into trust and inner steadiness, its faith in itself and in life stabilizing what was restless.
arrows.disintegration_text: Under stress the Six takes on average-to-unhealthy Three traits: competitive, image-conscious, and driven, overcompensating insecurity through performance.
arrows.source: Riso & Hudson, Personality Types (rev. 1996) & The Wisdom of the Enneagram (1999); enneagraminstitute.com. [STRUCTURE]. Exact pages CANNOT VERIFY.

arrows.integration_text: The scattered, acquisitive Seven becomes focused and deep, staying with one thing and finding satisfaction in depth rather than in more.
arrows.disintegration_text: Under stress the Seven takes on average-to-unhealthy One traits: critical, perfectionistic, impatient, and rigid as options close and pain cannot be outrun.
arrows.source: Riso & Hudson, Personality Types (rev. 1996) & The Wisdom of the Enneagram (1999); enneagraminstitute.com. [STRUCTURE]. Exact pages CANNOT VERIFY.

arrows.integration_text: The domineering, self-protective Eight lets the guard drop and turns its strength toward others, allowing care, generosity, and an open heart.
arrows.disintegration_text: Under stress the Eight takes on average-to-unhealthy Five traits: withdrawn, secretive, and isolated, retreating and conserving instead of confronting.
arrows.source: Riso & Hudson, Personality Types (rev. 1996) & The Wisdom of the Enneagram (1999); enneagraminstitute.com. [STRUCTURE]. Exact pages CANNOT VERIFY.

arrows.integration_text: The self-forgetting Nine invests in itself, shows up with energy and focus, and acts on its own priorities rather than merging with others'.
arrows.disintegration_text: Under stress the Nine takes on average-to-unhealthy Six traits: anxious, doubting, defensive, and dependent, clinging to support rather than staying asleep.
arrows.source: Riso & Hudson, Personality Types (rev. 1996) & The Wisdom of the Enneagram (1999); enneagraminstitute.com. [STRUCTURE]. Exact pages CANNOT VERIFY.
